title: List indexing: 1-based, negative from the end, NULL out of range and at 0
verdict: 1-based; the written SQL adds 1 to Substrait's 0-based offset
description: `l[i]` (`list_extract`, `list_element`) counts from 1; a negative index counts from the end (`[10, 20, 30][-1]` is 30, `[-3]` is 10). Index 0, an index past either end (`[4]`, `[-4]`, `2⁶³ − 1`), a NULL index and a NULL list give NULL, with no error.
Slices `l[a:b]` are 1-based and inclusive (`[2:3]` is `[20, 30]`, `[-2:]` the last two); `[0:1]` is `[10]` and an empty range is `[]`.
reference: Substrait's `ListElement` offset is 0-based, negative from the end, NULL out of range in either direction, without wrapping (`Value.listElement`, #94). DuckDB's SQL writes `l[i + 1]` for an offset `i ≥ 0` and `l[i]` for a negative one, which agree on every offset (docs/nested-values.md). `list_extract(l, i)` read from DuckDB SQL is `l[i]`, modelled exactly with a constant index (#327).
